h1: The 5 Best Glass Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Glass Air Fryers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best glass air fryers of 2026, from Ninja Crispi to Cuisinart and Kismile, compared by modes, size and price bucket.
summary: The Ninja Crispi Pro is the most capable glass air fryer here with 6 functions. The Ninja Crispi 4-in-1 is the balanced pick at $100-200. The Kismile 5QT is the cheaper way into glass, and the Cuisinart adds a ClearView window.
intro: Glass air fryers solve a real annoyance: you can watch food brown without opening the basket and letting heat escape. The catch is that glass models vary a lot in size, modes and price, and the product titles rarely tell you which differences matter.
We ranked five glass air fryers using only the details their listings give, such as function count, capacity and price bucket. Where a listing is thin, we say so.

products.name: Ninja Crispi Pro Glass Air Fryer
products.verdict: The widest feature set among glass models here.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi Pro is a glass air fryer with 6 functions, model AS101LG. Six modes means it can do more than air fry alone.

It ranks above the 4-in-1 Crispi because it adds two more functions, at the cost of landing in the $200-500 bucket.

Best for cooks who want one appliance to do the most. The caveat is the higher price bracket.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want maximum function in glass.
products.skipIf: You only want to air fry on a budget.

products.name: Ninja Crispi Glass Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 4-in-1 glass fryer in the middle price bucket.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi, model FN101GY, is a 4-in-1 glass air fryer in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks below the Pro for two fewer functions but above the cheaper picks for Ninja's four-mode design. The tradeoff is fewer modes than the Pro.

Best for buyers who want a Crispi without the premium. The caveat is that other listings of this model come in different colors, so confirm the model number.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a balanced glass fryer.

products.name: Ninja Crispi DualZone Glass Countertop Air Fryer
products.verdict: The DualZone name points to two cooking zones.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi DualZone is a glass countertop air fryer, model DD101IV2, in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks below the Pro because the listing gives no function count or capacity to justify the same price. The DualZone name suggests two zones, but the data we have does not spell out capacity.

Best for cooks curious about dual cooking. The caveat is little confirmed detail.
products.idealFor: Ninja fans interested in the DualZone design.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 4 Qt glass basket with a ClearView window.
products.description:
The Cuisinart air fryer has a glass basket and ClearView window, 5 functions and a 4 Qt capacity, in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks below the Ninja picks for the smaller 4 Qt size, but the window lets you watch food as it cooks. The tradeoff is capacity.

Best for one or two people. The caveat is the smaller basket.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples who like watching food cook.

products.name: Kismile 5QT Glass Air Fryer
products.description:
The Kismile is a 5QT glass air fryer in the $50-100 bucket, the lowest price band in this ranking.

It ranks last because the listing gives no function count or other features, but it has a larger 5QT capacity than the Cuisinart. The tradeoff is thin documentation.

Best for budget buyers wanting glass. The caveat is limited detail.
products.idealFor: Budget shoppers wanting a glass fryer.

whatMatters.detail: A 4-in-1 or 6-in-1 label counts cooking modes like air fry or roast. More modes replace other appliances. Look for the number in the title and confirm which modes are included.
Quarts describe how much food fits. 4 Qt suits one or two people, while 5QT feeds a little more. Check the quart size in the title.
Glass lets you watch browning without opening the unit. A ClearView window does the same. Look for glass named in the listing.
Ninja sells the Crispi under identical names with different model numbers and colors. Confirm the model like FN101GY. Check it in the title before ordering.
Glass models span from $50-100 to $200-500. Higher tiers add modes. Check the live price before buying.

faq.q: Why choose glass over a regular air fryer?
faq.a: You can watch food without opening the unit. That keeps heat in and helps avoid overcooking.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with the Ninja Crispi?
faq.a: They mix up model numbers. Several Crispi listings share a name but differ by model and color.

faq.q: Is the Crispi Pro worth it over the 4-in-1?
faq.a: If you will use six functions, yes. Otherwise the 4-in-1 in the $100-200 bucket is the better value.
It lists a 4 Qt capacity, which suits one or two people.

faq.q: How do I clean a glass air fryer?
faq.a: Check the manual for dishwasher safety and avoid abrasive pads on glass.

faq.q: Does the DualZone have two baskets?
faq.a: The name suggests two zones, but the listing does not give details, so confirm on the product page.

finalTake: The Ninja Crispi Pro is the best glass air fryer here for sheer capability, and the Ninja Crispi 4-in-1 is the balanced buy. The Cuisinart suits small households, and the Kismile is the low-cost entry. Confirm model numbers before ordering.
